title: Freeze-and-thaw of the rigid core
spec: After each restart's final SLSQP stage, identify the rigid core as the circles with at least three contacts within 1e-6 of tangency. For the next restart derived from the incumbent, freeze the centres and radii of the rigid core, re-randomise the centres and radii of the remaining rattlers and boundary-free circles uniformly in the square with radii 0.05, and re-run the radius-cap continuation with the core fixed as equality constraints for the first two stages. Then release the core and run the full continuation. Repeat this with a fresh random seed for the freed circles. This is a partial restart that keeps good structure while reopening the loose parts, which is different from a global perturbation.

title: Centre jitter between continuation stages
spec: After each radius-cap SLSQP stage, add Gaussian noise to the centres with standard deviation 0.02 times the current cap divided by 0.4, then clip to [0,1]. Run the next stage from the jittered point. The noise shrinks as the cap grows, so early stages explore and late stages refine. Keep the best final repaired packing across restarts as before.

title: Tabu search on a discrete occupancy grid, then SLSQP polish
spec: Before each SLSQP restart, discretise the unit square into a 40x40 grid of candidate centres. Place 26 circles on distinct cells with a tabu search: at each step, move one circle to a random nearby empty cell or swap two cells, score a layout by the sum over circles of the distance to the nearest other circle or wall (min-gap proxy), and keep a tabu list of the last 30 moves to avoid cycling. Run about 300 tabu steps from a random layout, take the best layout as the centre start for SLSQP, and use the cap-continuation schedule from the incumbent. Use the seed for all randomness. This replaces the uniform random centre start in a random half of the restarts.

title: Random aspect-ratio start that anneals to the square
spec: Give each restart a random rectangle of aspect ratio drawn log-uniformly from [0.8, 1.25], with width w and height h such that w times h equals 1. Place the initial centres uniformly inside this rectangle and run the radius-cap SLSQP continuation with the box constraints of the rectangle. Then, in a final stage, morph the box to the unit square by linearly interpolating the box bounds over five SLSQP solves, using the previous solution as the start each time. The final stage must satisfy the exact unit square bounds, so the repair step still applies. This is a container-side continuation that lets the packing reorganise through non-square intermediate shapes.

title: Damped molecular-dynamics inflation as a start
spec: Replace the uniform random start with a short damped particle simulation. Place 26 particles at random in the square with random small velocities. Each step, apply a soft repulsive force from pairwise overlaps (linear spring on max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)) and a wall spring, add a viscous damping term and a small thermostat kick from the seeded RNG, and grow all radii slowly toward a target of about 0.1 per step, capped at 0.2. Run about 400 steps with numpy vectorised pair forces, then pass the centres and radii to the existing SLSQP cap continuation. Keep the cost per restart small so that many restarts fit in the budget.

title: Batched projected-gradient population before SLSQP
spec: Each solve call first runs a vectorised numpy population of 64 starts at once. Each start has centres in [0,1]^2 and radii set to zero. Run about 300 steps of projected gradient ascent on the radius sum with a quadratic overlap penalty whose weight grows geometrically. Use numpy broadcasting over the population dimension, so each step costs one batched pairwise computation. Take the top 3 configurations by repaired radius sum, and run the existing SLSQP cap continuation only on those. Keep the time-budget loop, with the population stage counted inside TIME_FRACTION.

title: Poisson-disk cell-seeded starts
spec: On a random half of the restarts, generate the centre start with a dart-throwing Poisson-disk sampler on [0.05, 0.95]^2 using the seeded rng. Use a minimum spacing that starts at 0.2 and is reduced by a factor of 0.97 whenever 2000 attempts fail, until 26 points are placed. This gives an evenly spread start with a different structure from uniform noise. Assign each point the radius INIT_RADIUS and run the usual continuation. Keep the rest of the restart procedure and the repair step unchanged.

title: Sequential Apollonius-style greedy construction as a start
spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in some restarts with a greedy build. Shuffle the 26 indices with the seeded rng. For each circle in turn, evaluate a fixed grid of about 2000 candidate centres in [0,1]^2 (drawn from rng). For each candidate, the largest feasible radius is min(distance to each wall, distance to each placed centre minus its radius). Place the circle at the candidate with the largest feasible radius, and set its radius to that value times 0.9. The resulting centres and radii are the start for the usual SLSQP cap continuation. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Tolerance annealing across the continuation
spec: Keep the cap-continuation schedule but make the SLSQP tolerance part of it. Use a loose ftol of 1e-3 and a maximum of 40 iterations for the early caps (0.05 to 0.2), then ftol 1e-6 and 120 iterations for the middle caps, and ftol 1e-12 with the full MAX_ITER for the final cap of 1.0. The intent is to spend less CPU on early stages that only move circles into the right basin, so that more restarts fit into the 80 percent budget, while the final stage still converges tightly. Keep everything else identical to the incumbent, including the repair step.

title: Beta-distributed centre density for the random start
spec: Replace the uniform draw of the centres with a draw from a product of Beta distributions. For each restart, pick a shape pair (a, b) from a seeded set of values {(0.7, 0.7), (1.0, 1.0), (1.5, 1.5), (2.0, 2.0)}, then draw each centre coordinate from Beta(a, b) and map it into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. The shapes (a, b) below 1 push circles to the walls and shapes above 1 push them to the middle. Choose the shape at random per restart, so the search covers both wall-heavy and centre-heavy starts. The rest of the pipeline stays as it is.

title: Gaussian-mixture sampling of starts from the elite centres
spec: Maintain a small archive of the centres of the best 10 distinct packings found so far. For each new restart after the first five, draw the start from a fitted isotropic Gaussian mixture: pick one archived packing at random, take its centre set, and add N(0, 0.05) jitter to every centre with a 0.2 probability of replacing one centre by a uniform random point. Clip to [0.05, 0.95] and assign radii of 0.05. Use only numpy and the seed. This turns the elite pool into a sampling density over starts instead of a list of parents for crossover, so the search concentrates on regions that already produced good sums.

title: Dual-multiplier-guided perturbation of the incumbent
spec: After the first 40 restarts, take the incumbent and its SLSQP constraint multipliers from the last solve, which scipy returns as res.jac for the active set (the multiplier of constraint k is estimated from the gradient of the objective against the active constraint Jacobians with a least-squares solve). Rank circles by the sum of multipliers of their active contacts. Re-randomise the centres of the 3 circles with the smallest sum, which are the least constrained, to uniform positions in [0.1, 0.9]^2. Keep all other circles fixed at their incumbent positions, then run the normal continuation SLSQP with a cap starting at the incumbent's smallest radius. Accept the result only if it beats the incumbent.

title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth as a start
spec: Replace the uniform random centres in each restart with a short growth simulation. Start 26 points at random positions with radius 0.01. Repeat 400 steps: give each circle a random displacement of size 0.02 times a shrinking step factor, reject any displacement that creates an overlap, then grow every radius by a factor of 1.002 up to the largest value that keeps the packing feasible given the current neighbours. Use the resulting centres and radii as the start of the SLSQP continuation. Use the seed to make the random moves reproducible. The step factor halves every 100 steps, so the growth finishes in a near-jammed state.

title: Random dihedral image of the incumbent as a restart seed
spec: On every fourth restart, take the best packing found so far in this solve call and apply one of the eight symmetries of the square chosen at random by the seeded rng: identity, the three rotations, and the four reflections. Apply the transform to the centres, keep the radii, add Gaussian noise of 0.01 to the centres, clip to the box, and use the result as the start for the cap continuation from cap 0.05 onward, with the radii taken from the transformed incumbent. This reuses structure of the good packing while letting the continuation move every circle.

title: Two-stage multi-start with a shared starting pool of 200 centres
spec: At the start of solve, draw a pool of 200 random centre sets with the seed, and score each one by a fast penalty energy, the sum of squared pair overlaps at a fixed radius of 0.09, computed in a single vectorised numpy call on the stacked (200, 26, 2) array. Sort the pool by energy and run the full SLSQP continuation on the 40 lowest-energy starts in order, until the time budget is used. Replace the random uniform draw in the restart loop with this pool. The batch scoring costs a few milliseconds and needs no extra solver, and it gives the continuation a better-ordered set of starts.

title: Vectorised perturbation screen of the incumbent
spec: Each call, after the first restart, generate 400 candidate perturbations of the best packing's centres (Gaussian noise with a random scale in [0.005, 0.1] per candidate). Score every candidate in one batched numpy pass with a cheap feasible-radius proxy: start from r_i = min(wall distance), then 5 vectorised fixed-point sweeps of r_i = min(r_i, min_j (d_ij - r_j)) over the batch, and sum the radii. Run SLSQP (the existing cap continuation) only on the top 3 candidates and keep the best result. Leave the random restarts unchanged for the other part of the budget.

title: Two-sided cap continuation with free stages
spec: Extend the radius-cap continuation so that after each cap stage a short free SLSQP stage runs with the cap removed but the radii bounded by the previous cap plus 0.02. Alternate capped and free stages: capped at 0.05, free, capped at 0.07, free, and so on up to 0.4, then one final uncapped stage. The free stages let circles that were held back by the cap move again, while the cap keeps the early geometry coherent. Limit each free stage to 30 SLSQP iterations.

title: Square-grid-with-defects initialisation
spec: Add a start family that places 26 circles on a 5x5 grid with one extra point, or on a 6x5 grid with 4 points removed, chosen at random from seed. Scale the grid to fill [0.1, 0.9], add uniform jitter of amplitude 0.05 to every centre, and set initial radii to 0.05. Use this start for half the restarts and the existing uniform start for the rest. This is a different lattice from the hexagonal start, and the defects give the continuation a broken symmetry to relax.

title: Parallel-tempering start generator on overlap energy
spec: Before each SLSQP restart, run a small parallel-tempering pool of 6 replicas of the 26 centres in the unit square. Each replica minimises the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 plus wall overlaps, with radii fixed at a common value that is slowly raised. Use a temperature ladder from 1e-4 to 1e-2 geometric. Each sweep does Metropolis moves of size 0.05 times the replica's temperature rank, followed by swap attempts between neighbouring temperatures every 10 sweeps. Run for a fixed budget of 300 sweeps and feed the lowest-energy replica's centres into SLSQP. This gives an annealed, physically motivated start instead of a uniform draw.

title: Radius-class tying for a reduced parametrisation
spec: In each restart, assign the 26 circles to K=3 radius classes with a random class sizes drawn from a Dirichlet prior. Optimise over centres and K class radii only, so the variable count drops from 3n to 2n+K. Constraints are written per pair using the class radius of each circle. After convergence, run one free SLSQP polish with all n radii starting from the tied solution. The tied stage explores a smaller and more structured space, and the free polish recovers the full optimum. Keep the existing cap continuation in the tied stage.

title: Least-squares overlap residuals with trust-region reflective solver
spec: Replace the SLSQP call in each restart with scipy.optimize.least_squares using method 'trf'. Variables are the centres and radii. The residual vector contains max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij) for all pairs i<j, max(0, r_i - x_i), max(0, r_i - y_i), max(0, x_i + r_i - 1), max(0, y_i + r_i - 1), plus a penalty of minus a weight times r_i that drives radii to grow. Use a weight that increases from 0.01 to 1 over three solves with the same start, and at the end run one SLSQP pass with a short iteration cap to clean up contacts. This keeps the local solver different from the current constrained optimiser while still using the same restart loop and repair step.

title: Feasibility-form SLSQP with a sum constraint
spec: Add an alternative local solver for some restarts. Fix a target T for the radius sum, starting at the incumbent's sum times 1.0 from the first best packing found. Solve the feasibility problem: minimise the sum of squared centre-pair overlaps plus squared wall violations, subject to sum(r) >= T and the cap constraints, with SLSQP. If the solver reports success, raise T by 0.002 and repeat from the solution. If it fails, lower T by 0.001. Stop when the step is below 0.0005 or the time slice is used. Pass the best feasible packing through the existing repair step.

title: Soft container-wall repulsion annealed to zero
spec: During the first two cap-continuation stages of each restart, add to the SLSQP objective a soft wall penalty of the form 0.02 times the sum of exp(-(distance to wall minus radius)/0.02) over all circles and four walls, with an analytic gradient. Linearly reduce the coefficient to zero over those two stages so the final stages optimise the true sum of radii. This regulariser acts only on the container edges, unlike the pair Coulomb penalty already tried.

title: Two-scale hole-targeted restart
spec: After the first restart, each later restart takes the best packing and removes its two smallest-radius circles. It then places each removed circle at the largest empty hole, found as the Voronoi vertex with the greatest distance to the nearest centre inside the unit square, and gives both circles a random radius at most 0.5 of that hole's distance. Run the usual radius-cap continuation on the resulting configuration. This is a targeted change to a near-optimal start, and it differs from random insertion by picking holes deterministically.

title: Maximin-spread centre start
spec: Before each SLSQP restart, replace the uniform random centres with a maximin-spread configuration: solve max t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t and wall margins >= 0.05, using SLSQP over the 2n centre coordinates plus t, started from a random layout, with 100 iterations. Use the resulting centres as the start for the usual radius-cap continuation, with radii initialised to 0.5 times the distance to the nearest neighbour. Only the start changes; the rest of the restart is identical.

title: Island model with elite migration
spec: Split the restart budget across four islands, each with its own fixed radius-cap schedule (for example one coarse, one fine, one with an extra free stage, one with a geometric grid). Each island keeps its own best packing. Every fixed number of restarts, copy the best packing of one island into the start pool of another, chosen at random with a seeded RNG, and use it as a warm start for one restart. Return the overall best packing, repaired as before. The islands keep the search diverse while migration spreads good basins.

title: Largest-hole hopping on converged packings
spec: After each restart converges, find the largest empty circle: evaluate a 300 by 300 grid over the square, compute the distance to the nearest centre minus its radius, and take the grid point with the largest free clearance. Move the circle with the smallest Lagrange-multiplier-weighted contact load (or the smallest radius if multipliers are unavailable) to that point, set its radius to the clearance, and rerun the radius-cap SLSQP continuation from the new configuration. Keep the move only if the total radius sum rises. Apply this at most three times per restart.

title: Stall-triggered early abort of SLSQP
spec: Wrap each SLSQP call with a callback that records the objective after every iteration. If the objective has improved by less than 1e-6 over the last 15 iterations and the constraint violation is below 1e-4, raise a private StopEarly exception caught around the minimize call and keep the last feasible iterate. This cuts time spent on converged-but-slow restarts, freeing the budget for more starts. Keep the MAX_ITER cap as an upper bound and make sure the final returned packing is still repaired before comparison.

title: Langevin sampling of centres with LP-optimal radii as energy
spec: Treat the energy of a centre set as minus the optimal sum of radii, where the radii come from a fast LP (HiGHS linprog) with the pair and wall constraints. Run a short overdamped Langevin walk on the centres with Gaussian steps whose scale decays geometrically over the iterations, accepting moves by Metropolis with a temperature that also decays. Keep the best feasible centre set seen. Run SLSQP once on that best set at the end of the walk. The walk is a global search over the centre landscape, independent of SLSQP's local basin.

title: Cheap batch-vectorised screening of initial configurations
spec: Before each SLSQP restart, generate 64 random starts as a single numpy array and compute, in one vectorised pass, the minimum pairwise gap and the sum of feasible radii that a greedy radius assignment gives for each start. Only the best 4 starts by this score go through the full radius-cap SLSQP. Keep the time check and the repair step unchanged. This batches the cheap screening work across starts so most CPU time goes to the few candidates that look promising.

title: Centroid-pull regulariser on centres
spec: Add a small quadratic term beta * sum_i ||c_i - (0.5, 0.5)||^2 to the minimised objective during the early cap stages, with beta = 0.02 decaying linearly to zero over the first half of the cap schedule. This biases the continuation toward compact layouts where radii can grow in the middle, and leaves the feasible set untouched. Final stages use the true objective, so the returned packing is optimal for the unregularised problem.

title: Block-coordinate SLSQP on random subsets
spec: After each restart's global SLSQP stage, repeat 6 times: choose a random subset of 8 circles, fix all other centres and radii, and run SLSQP over only the subset's centres and radii with the full constraint set (fixed circles appear as constants). Accept the block update only if the total radius sum rises, then finish with one full SLSQP pass. This decomposes the problem into small local solves that can escape configurations a global solve cannot leave.

title: Interior-point log-barrier stage
spec: Solve the radius maximisation with a log-barrier method: minimise minus the sum of radii minus mu times the sum of log of all slack values (pair and boundary), with mu decreasing from 1e-1 to 1e-7 over about six Newton stages using scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr or BFGS. Use the result as the warm start for a short SLSQP run. The barrier keeps iterates strictly feasible, which avoids the repair step on many starts.

title: Dihedral-symmetry transforms of the incumbent as restarts
spec: After the first restart, take the best packing found so far and apply each of the 8 symmetries of the square (identity, the 3 rotations, and 4 reflections, mapping centres by (x, y) to (x, y), (y, 1-x), (1-x, 1-y), (1-y, x), and the reflections). Run the radius-cap SLSQP continuation from each transformed copy with its radii as the start, then repair and keep the best. Those transforms give the same packing, so this step only helps if the local solver reaches a different basin from a slightly different start. Add small Gaussian jitter of scale 0.01 to the centres before the solve, using the seeded rng, to make the copies differ. Use this branch for about one quarter of the time budget and random restarts for the rest.

title: Torus-relaxed start
spec: Before the SLSQP restart, relax the 26 centres on a unit torus: minimise a soft overlap energy where distances use the minimum-image convention, so there are no walls. Use a short L-BFGS-B run from the uniform random start with a seeded RNG. Then map the torus configuration into [0,1]^2 by a random translation and a rescale toward the centre so that the wall terms are satisfied, and hand that start to the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation. The torus removes boundary effects, so the start tends to a bulk-like lattice pattern. Keep the repair step as is.

title: Two-stage ladder from 24 and 28 optima
spec: Each restart solves a packing for 24 circles and one for 28 circles with the existing cap continuation. Take the 28-circle packing and remove the two circles of smallest radius (or the two whose removal leaves the best sum after one SLSQP polish). Take the 24-circle packing and insert two circles at the two largest holes found by a 200 by 200 grid search. Polish both candidates with the usual final SLSQP stage and keep the better one. This is a bolder ladder that brackets 26 from both sides.

title: Soft-mode kick along low vibrational modes
spec: Build the contact network of the incumbent (pairs with gap below 1e-6 plus wall contacts). Form the linearised stiffness matrix of the overlap energy over the 2n centre coordinates and take its lowest non-zero eigenvectors, which are the soft modes. For each new restart after the first, perturb the incumbent centres along a random combination of the 3 softest modes with amplitude drawn from [0.02, 0.06], clip to the box, then run the radius-cap continuation from the repaired perturbed packing. Keep the usual best-of-restarts rule.

title: Cluster rotation move on the incumbent
spec: On every other restart after the first, pick a random centre c0 in the square and a radius R in [0.2, 0.45]. Take all circles whose centres lie within R of c0 and rotate their centres about c0 by a random angle in [-30, 30] degrees, leaving the others fixed. Clip to the box, repair the radii, and run only the last two stages of the radius-cap continuation (caps 0.3 and 1.0) to re-settle. Keep the best packing by sum of radii.

title: Saddle escape via negative curvature of the Lagrangian
spec: After each restart's final SLSQP stage, form the Hessian of the Lagrangian (objective plus active-contact multipliers, taken from the SLSQP result or estimated by least squares on the KKT residual) over the centres and radii, restricted to the active set. If its smallest eigenvalue is negative, step along the corresponding eigenvector by a small amount (about 0.01) in both signs, re-run the radius-cap final stage from each perturbed point, and keep the best sum. Skip the step when no negative curvature is found, so the cost is one eigen-decomposition per restart.

title: Pairwise margin annealing to zero
spec: Replace the constraint d_ij >= r_i + r_j in the cap continuation by d_ij >= (r_i + r_j)(1 + eps_k) where eps_k decreases geometrically from 0.02 at the first stage to 0 at the final stage. The margin keeps early stages strictly feasible with spare room for reorganisation, and it is removed before the last stage so the final packing is tight. Keep the repair step unchanged as the last safety net.

title: Per-circle random objective weights during continuation
spec: In each _solve_once, draw a fixed weight w_i uniformly in [0.9, 1.1] per circle from rng. For every cap stage except the last, maximise sum(w_i * r_i) instead of sum(r_i). Run the final cap=1.0 stage with uniform weights so the returned objective is the true sum of radii. The weights break the symmetry of the early optima so different restarts land in different basins, without changing the final objective.

title: Annealed random tilt of the objective
spec: Add a term -eps_k * (a . c) to the SLSQP objective, where a is a random unit vector per restart drawn from rng, c is the flattened centre vector, and eps_k decays geometrically from 0.05 to 0 across the cap-continuation stages, so the last stage is the unmodified sum-of-radii problem. The tilt breaks the symmetry of the uniform start and pushes the early stages toward distinct basins without changing the final objective. Keep the Jacobian of the tilt term analytic and the rest of the code unchanged.

title: Wall-side rotated restart frame
spec: For a random third of the restarts, rotate the whole initial layout by a random angle theta in [0, pi/4] about (0.5, 0.5) before SLSQP, then clip the centres to [0, 1] and set radii to INIT_RADIUS. Because the square is not rotationally symmetric, the initial layout meets the walls at different angles, which changes which circles start in the corners. Leave the rest of the optimiser and the repair unchanged. This is a bounded-rotation variant of the dihedral transforms already tested, so it is not a copy of them.

title: Two-speed restart timing
spec: Split the CPU budget into a 'scout' phase using the first 25 percent of TIME_FRACTION * time_limit and a 'deep' phase using the rest. In the scout phase run ordinary restarts with MAX_ITER set to 60. Then take the top 3 packings by sum and run each through the full cap continuation with MAX_ITER set to 200, using the remaining time, keeping the best. This is a deterministic two-speed schedule without bandit weights, and it differs from successive halving in that the survivors get an additional full continuation rather than a single extra stage.

title: Cut-and-splice crossover on the elite pool
spec: Keep the best 6 distinct packings found so far. For a restart after the first two, choose two parents at random from the pool. Draw a random line through the unit square, and take the circles of parent A on one side and parent B on the other. Count the circles on each side, then fix the total at 26 by deleting a random circle from the surplus side or inserting a random point in the largest gap on the deficit side. Use the spliced centres as the start for the radius-cap SLSQP continuation. Standard Deaven-Ho cut-and-splice: the crossover is a geometric cut, not a value blend.

title: Partial-update restarts from the incumbent
spec: For every fifth restart, start from the incumbent's centres and reset only a random subset of 8 circles to uniform random positions. Keep the other 18 centres and all radii from the incumbent, then run the radius-cap continuation with the cap starting at 0.12 instead of 0.05, since the kept circles already have large radii. Take the best packing over all restarts as before. This is a batch-level restart mix: the bulk of each start is the incumbent and the randomness is a local partial reset, which is different from the full-perturbation basin hopping already rejected.

title: Quasi-crystal patch start
spec: On a random half of the restarts, build the initial centres from a patch of a quasi-periodic tiling: take points from a 2D cut-and-project construction with a random irrational slope and offset, keep the 26 points nearest to the square centre, then rescale them to fill [0.1, 0.9]^2. Give the others the existing uniform random start. Jitter all centres by a small seeded Gaussian. Starts from a quasi-periodic order are non-lattice and can reach configurations that hexagonal and square starts miss.

title: Concentric ring seeding around the square centre
spec: For a random third of the restarts, build the initial centres as concentric rings about (0.5, 0.5). Draw a ring count K from {2, 3, 4}, split the 26 circles into rings with counts drawn at random summing to 26 (each ring at least 1), place ring k at radius proportional to k with a random global scale in [0.25, 0.4], and offset each ring by an independent random angle. Add Gaussian jitter of 0.01 to every coordinate and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Pass the result to the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation unchanged.

title: Rattler jiggle after convergence
spec: After each SLSQP local optimum, identify rattlers as circles whose radius is well below the average and whose pair slacks are all positive. Give each rattler a random displacement of about 0.05 and rerun SLSQP. Repeat for three rounds, keeping the best packing. Rattlers carry no weight in the optimum, so this moves them into better positions without changing the rest.

title: Gauge-normalised objective with a radius-ratio penalty
spec: Add a small regularisation term to the cap-continuation SLSQP objective: minus the sum of radii plus lambda times the variance of the radii, with lambda set to 0.02 during the first half of the cap schedule and 0 afterwards. The variance term discourages early freezing of one large circle and a crowd of tiny ones, which tends to trap SLSQP. Analytic gradient is simple: the derivative of the variance with respect to each radius is 2 (r_i - mean) / n. Keep the constraints, repair, and best-of selection unchanged.

title: Cross-entropy adaptation of start distributions
spec: Parametrise the random initial-centre distribution as a Beta(a, b) product over the square with per-axis parameters, plus a radius-start mean. Start with a=b=1 and the current radius start. Each generation, draw 20 starts, run the existing SLSQP cap continuation on each, and record the repaired sum. Refit a and b (and the radius mean) by moment matching to the top 25 percent of starts, with a small floor on the variance so the distribution never collapses to a point. Iterate generations until the time budget is spent, always keeping the overall best packing. All draws use rng from the seed.

title: Metropolis walk over contact graphs
spec: After the first restart, run a Metropolis chain on the best packing's contact graph. A move picks one active contact at random and removes it by slightly separating its two circles (a random displacement of about 0.02 along the contact normal). It then re-solves the cap continuation starting from a small number of SLSQP iterations (about 80) and accepts the new packing with probability min(1, exp((S_new - S_old)/T)). Set T to 0.002 and decay it geometrically to 0.0002 over the remaining budget. Keep the best packing seen. This explores neighbouring contact topologies rather than resampling centres from scratch.

title: Spread-then-LP start generator
spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in half of the restarts with a max-min spreading stage. Solve SLSQP on variables (centres, t) to maximise t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t^2 for all pairs and t/2 <= c_i <= 1 - t/2 coordinate-wise, starting from a random layout. Then fix the centres and solve an exact LP with scipy linprog (HiGHS) for radii: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= x_i, r_i <= y_i, r_i <= 1 - x_i, r_i <= 1 - y_i, r >= 0. Feed the (centres, LP radii) pair into the existing radius-cap continuation. Keep the rest of solve() unchanged and seed all randomness from rng.

title: Noise-scaled restarts from the incumbent's radius profile
spec: On every second restart after the first, build the start by taking the current best packing's radius profile, sorting it, and assigning the sorted values to a fresh random permutation of the centres. Multiply each radius by a factor exp(0.3 * z) with z standard normal, clipped to a range of 0.5 to 1.5. Keep centres uniform on [0.1, 0.9] as in the original start. Then run the cap continuation and repair as usual. This keeps the size statistics of the best packing while randomising the geometry, which is a different start family from the previous ones tried.

title: Reversed cap continuation from large to small
spec: Run the radius-cap continuation in the opposite direction. Start from a random uniform packing with caps of 1.0, then reduce the cap through 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, and 0.15 down to 0.1 and keep the final stage uncapped at 1.0 for polishing. The reversal lets the largest circles settle first and forces the small ones to fill the gaps, which is the opposite of the current small-to-large schedule. Keep the number of stages and iteration cap per stage similar to the incumbent. Select between the forward and reversed schedule by a coin flip from the seed, so both are represented across restarts.

title: Trust-constr polish of the final best packing
spec: After all random restarts, take the best packing and refine it with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr. Pass the same objective and constraints as the SLSQP solver, supply the constraints as a NonlinearConstraint with the sparse pair-index arrays, and set a gradient-free default for the Hessian. Run it with a fixed maximum number of iterations and keep its result only if its sum of radii is larger and the repair step passes. Reserve about 10 percent of the time budget for this polish, and reduce the restart time to match.

title: Population restarts with batched LP radius scoring
spec: Generate 40 random centre layouts per batch with the usual uniform start. For each layout, compute the radii by solving the LP that maximises the sum of radii subject to pairwise and wall constraints, using a single HiGHS linprog call on the fixed centres. Score each layout by its LP sum. Keep the top 3 layouts and run the full cap continuation SLSQP on those only. Repeat batches until 60 percent of the CPU budget is used, then spend the rest on the best-so-far continuation. This puts an exact cheap screen in front of the expensive solver.

title: Quadrant decomposition and global merge
spec: For each restart, split the 26 circles at random into four groups by assigning them to quadrants of the unit square using their random starting centres. Solve each quadrant as a separate packing inside its own square with the radius-cap SLSQP, then rescale the four local solutions into their quadrants and use the merged configuration as the start for one global radius-cap SLSQP run. This is a coarse-to-fine move that builds the layout from local blocks rather than a single random start.

title: Chebyshev square-relaxation start
spec: Before the circle SLSQP, solve a relaxed problem in which every circle is an axis-aligned square of half-side r_i. Maximise sum r_i subject to the square-square non-overlap written as max(|x_i-x_j|, |y_i-y_j|) >= r_i + r_j, handled smoothly by requiring either the x or the y separation, with a random sign-pattern choice per pair seeded by rng, and the box constraints r_i <= x_i <= 1 - r_i. Use the resulting centres (and radii scaled to be feasible) as the starting point of the usual circle continuation. This gives a different contact topology from uniform random starts while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Adaptive per-restart convergence budget
spec: Track how many SLSQP restarts end with res.success true and how many hit the maxiter cap. Start with MAX_ITER=200 and ftol=1e-6. If the fraction hitting the cap is above 0.3, raise MAX_ITER by 50 for the next restart, up to 600. If the fraction is below 0.05, lower it by 25, down to 100. Also tighten the SLSQP ftol to 1e-9 for the final cap stage only. Stop the schedule when the time budget is used. This spends the budget where convergence is actually the bottleneck instead of using one fixed iteration limit everywhere.

title: Cone-lifted circle formulation
spec: Re-express the problem with the radius of each circle represented as the height of a cone over the square. Start from the current random centres and set each radius to its distance to the nearest container wall. Then run SLSQP on the same objective, but add the pairwise constraint d_ij >= r_i + r_j only for pairs whose centres are within 2.5 times the current mean radius, and recompute the pair set once per cap stage. This is a different constraint topology from the full pair set and from the sparse neighbour list, and it lets the search reshape the contact graph between stages. Keep the exact repair step unchanged.

title: Global differential evolution on a smooth penalty
spec: For the first 25 percent of each call's time budget, run scipy differential_evolution over the 26 centres only (52 variables, bounds in [0,1]). The objective is the negative sum of radii computed greedily as the largest radii consistent with the centres (r_i = min of wall clearances and half the nearest-neighbour distances) minus a 100 times squared-overlap penalty, with popsize 15 and maxiter capped so the stage stops by its time budget. Then pass the best population member through the existing cap-continuation SLSQP and repair. Use seed-derived rng for DE so results are reproducible.

title: Voronoi-inradius per-circle radius caps
spec: For each start, compute the Voronoi diagram of the initial centres, clipped to the unit square (use a dense grid of 200 by 200 points to find each cell's nearest-site membership). Set each circle's radius cap in the cap-continuation to half its cell's approximate inradius, that is the distance from the centre to the farthest point of its cell, times a factor of 0.9. Use these per-circle caps instead of the uniform cap in the early stages, and switch to the uniform schedule for the last stage. The caps keep the early configuration spread out, so SLSQP does not collapse circles into one corner.

title: Shirley-Chiu disc-to-square start distribution
spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in _solve_once for a random half of the restarts by a Shirley-Chiu map of uniform points on the unit disc: sample u, v uniform on [0,1], map to the square [-1,1]^2 and then to a disc-shaped set, and rescale to [0.1, 0.9]^2 with a uniform random rotation. This gives a rounder, centre-weighted start that differs in shape from the square-uniform start. Keep the radius start, the cap schedule and the repair unchanged, and use the same rng for every draw so that seeds are reproducible.

title: Weight-decayed radii objective
spec: Add a small term to the SLSQP objective that penalises the spread of radii, for example minus the sum of radii plus 0.01 times the variance of radii, during the first half of the iterations. Set the weight to zero for the final SLSQP call. The early spread penalty pushes the search toward more uniform sizes that tend to pack densely, and removing it at the end keeps the true objective.

title: Final SLSQP polish with tight tolerance
spec: After the time loop finds the best packing, run one more SLSQP call started from it with ftol set to 1e-15 and a higher maxiter (for example 1000). Keep the result only if it is valid and its radius sum is higher. This recovers the last digits of the local optimum that the normal 200-iteration runs leave on the table.

title: Contact-count stopping rule for the cap continuation
spec: In _solve_once, after each cap stage compute the number of active contacts, meaning pair constraints with |d - r_i - r_j| < 1e-6 plus wall contacts with |wall gap| < 1e-6. If the active count is identical for two consecutive stages and the radius sum changed by less than 1e-4, skip the remaining cap stages and jump directly to the cap 1.0 stage. Track the number of restarts that finish early and report it only in a debug variable. The aim is to spend the freed CPU time on more restarts, since many late stages change almost nothing.
